questions.question: Why can psoriasis with limited body-surface area still be clinically severe?
choices: Small plaques are never symptomatic
Hands, feet, scalp, nails, face, genitals, pain, fissures, and quality-of-life burden can cause major disability
Body-surface area is the only severity measure
Psoriasis never affects work or mood
questions.explanation: Severity is more than body surface area. Special-site disease, pain, itch, fissures, nail involvement, work limitations, sexual health, sleep, and mental-health impact can make limited-area disease severe.

questions.question: Which symptom pattern should raise concern for psoriatic arthritis?
choices: Prolonged morning stiffness, swollen digits, heel pain, or inflammatory back symptoms
A stable asymptomatic freckle
Brief itch after bathing
One day of muscle soreness after exercise
questions.explanation: Persistent inflammatory stiffness, swollen joints, dactylitis, enthesitis, and inflammatory axial symptoms can signal psoriatic arthritis and warrant assessment and referral to prevent joint damage.

questions.question: Which is an appropriate FNP role in psoriasis care?
choices: Treat psoriasis as skin-only disease and ignore comorbidities
Assess cardiometabolic and mental-health risk and coordinate dermatology or rheumatology care when needed
Abruptly stop all specialist-directed systemic therapies
Assume all scaly plaques have the same cause
questions.explanation: Psoriasis is multisystem inflammatory disease. Primary care plays a key role in comorbidity assessment, medication coordination, preventive care, and timely specialty referral.

questions.question: Which presentation requires urgent evaluation rather than routine topical adjustment?
choices: Stable plaque psoriasis with mild itch
Diffuse painful erythema with fever, tachycardia, dehydration, or widespread pustules
A small unchanged scalp plaque
A request for moisturizer advice
questions.explanation: Erythroderma, generalized pustular disease, systemic illness, severe infection, or drug reaction can be dangerous. These patterns require urgent assessment.

questions.question: Why should a clinician reconsider the diagnosis when a presumed psoriasis plaque repeatedly fails reasonable treatment?
choices: All treatment failure proves the patient did not adhere
Tinea, dermatitis, drug eruption, infection, or another disorder may mimic psoriasis
Psoriasis always resolves after one application
More potent treatment is always safer than reassessment
questions.explanation: Persistent nonresponse should trigger review of diagnosis, treatment technique, access, and mimics. Escalating therapy without reassessment can delay correct care.

questions.question: Which finding supports screening for psoriatic arthritis even if skin plaques are stable?
choices: New whole-digit swelling and reduced hand function
A normal eye examination last year
A stable old scar
A preference for fragrance-free cleanser
questions.explanation: Dactylitis and functional decline can indicate inflammatory joint disease. Skin and joint activity may not change together, so joint screening should be deliberate.

questions.question: What is a common first-line principle for limited plaque psoriasis?
choices: Use site-appropriate topical therapy with clear duration and safety instructions
Use indefinite high-potency corticosteroids on all sites without review
Start biologic therapy without diagnosis confirmation
Avoid all moisturizers
questions.explanation: Topical treatment is often appropriate for limited disease, but potency, location, duration, adverse effects, and response must be reviewed. Thin or intertriginous skin requires different caution from thick plaques.

questions.question: A patient with psoriasis develops a painful red eye with photophobia and reduced vision. What is the priority?
choices: Prompt eye-care or emergency evaluation
A routine skin follow-up in six months
A stronger topical psoriasis medication only
Reassurance because eye symptoms are unrelated
questions.explanation: Painful red eye, photophobia, or visual change can indicate sight-threatening ocular disease and needs prompt evaluation rather than routine dermatology management.

questions.question: Which statement about systemic psoriasis therapy is most accurate for FNP practice?
choices: It can be selected without reviewing infection, reproductive, and comorbidity context
It requires diagnosis confirmation, safety planning, and dermatology coordination when indicated
It eliminates the need for preventive care
It should be stopped abruptly whenever a flare occurs
questions.explanation: Systemic and biologic therapies involve phenotype, infection, vaccine, pregnancy, hepatic, bowel, and other safety considerations. Coordination with specialists is essential.

questions.question: What does closed-loop specialty referral mean for a patient with psoriasis and inflammatory joint symptoms?
choices: Place a generic referral and assume care occurred
Document the concern and urgency, help ensure rheumatology access, review the recommendation, and clarify follow-up responsibilities
Wait for irreversible joint changes to confirm diagnosis
Tell the patient joint symptoms are cosmetic
questions.explanation: Closed-loop referral turns a consult order into actual coordinated care. This is especially important when delayed psoriatic arthritis recognition can permit joint damage.
